# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 60 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 60 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_060_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 6 — Why the Servant Did More Than Required

**60:1** "Lord," I said, "why did the slave do more than he was told? He was only ordered to fence the vineyard, but he also dug it and cleared it. What does that extra work represent?" "Listen," he said. "The slave is the Son of God, and the work he did beyond the commandment represents what he chose to do beyond what was strictly required of him."

**60:2** "You see, the Son of God wasn't content just to give the people commandments — he also carried their sins himself. That is what the additional work represents: the Son of God bearing the sins of the people and suffering on their behalf."

**60:3** "When he then consulted with the first-created angels about what reward the slave should receive for that extra work — that consultation is about the flesh of the Son of God. The flesh served the Spirit well and purely, completely free from defilement throughout its time on earth. That is why it was given a reward."

**60:4** "The Father consulted with the Son and the holy angels so that this flesh — which had served the Spirit without any fault — would receive a place to rest and not lose the reward for its service. Because every piece of flesh found pure and spotless, in which the Holy Spirit has lived, will receive a reward."

**60:5** "There you have the full interpretation of this parable." "I have it, lord," I said. "May I ask one more thing, lord?" "Go ahead," he said. "Lord," I said, "isn't flesh fragile and mortal?" "It is," he said. "But here's the thing: this mortal nature cannot be clothed with immortality unless the Holy Spirit first joins it. A person simply cannot wear immortality without first being clothed in the Holy Spirit. So — first clothe yourself in the Holy Spirit; then clothe yourself in the flesh; and the flesh will become subject to the Spirit."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, making the Spirit-flesh anthropology of Hermas's christology accessible.*
